title: products.yaml — how a ticket becomes code, an environment and a verdict
description: The registry that makes one loop serve every application. A ticket resolves to repos, a branch, a stack profile and test commands from here alone, with no human looking anything up.

match.description: How a ticket resolves to this product. At least one criterion must be present, or every ticket matches everything.

repos.description: owner/name. Every repo listed is cloned by the registry check and must carry the plugin, AGENTS.md and REVIEW.md.

multi_repo.description: When true, plan.md must produce per-repo tasks and a merge order, and nothing merges until every PR in the set is approved.

version_source.description: Where the resolved version comes from for a bug (e.g. a Jira field or a customer profile key). Absent means the branch policy alone decides.

forward_port.description: When a bug was fixed on a release branch, cherry-pick onto this branch as a draft PR. Conflicts escalate rather than silently skip.

topology_default.description: e.g. 2node. Per-process state is not a correctness mechanism above 1node.

liquibase.description: Whether the stack supports tag/rollbackToTag between attempts.

build.description: Build command. Absent means the product needs no build step before tests.

atdd.description: Must emit xunit. The build loop parses a verdict, it does not grep logs.

regression.description: Named suite for the product's full regression.

ui_trace.description: Absent means UI evidence is legitimately n/a for this product.

compose_test.description: Infra oracle: a check that fails on current state and is idempotent when applied twice.

owners.description: Owner group per blast-radius label. money and protocol must be named for any product that has such paths.

images.description: GHCR container package names (org alepolab) this product actually publishes, confirmed against `gh api /orgs/alepolab/packages?package_type=container` and the package's own repository link — not assumed from the repo name. Repo name is not image name (lum-selfcare-v1 -> lum-selfcare), and one repo commonly publishes several images (pms -> pms-billing, pms-partner-management, pms-ratingengine). May be empty only when version.strategy is "none" and no image has been catalogued yet; the registry check fails a non-empty-required case, see validate-registry.mjs.

version.description: How a version named in a ticket (read from the whole issue: fields, description, comments) maps to a resolvable ref for this product's images.

strategy.description: semver_tag: a vMAJOR.MINOR.PATCH (optionally -rc.N/-debug/-beta.N) tag identifies a release. branch_date_sha: tags are <branch>-<yyyymmdd>-<shortsha>; there is no release-number tag, so a ticket version must be resolved to a date/sha from the ticket's own evidence, not guessed. versioned_image_name: the version is baked into the GHCR *package name* itself (one package per release, e.g. aaa-server-14.0.3-oel9-mysql) rather than into a tag on a shared package. none: no image published by this product carries anything version-shaped, at any evidence level found — the pipeline MUST halt and escalate rather than default to a branch.

hint.description: Optional. The concrete tag/package shape actually observed for this product (with an example), and what to disregard (nightly/CI tags that are not a release version). Disambiguates which image and which token in a ticket is 'the version' for this product specifically.

upgrade_policy.description: can_upgrade: if the reported bug is already fixed on a later version than the customer runs, halt the run and recommend the upgrade instead of backporting. pinned: this product's customers cannot generally take an upgrade on demand, so always continue to a backport even when the fix already shipped later. both: depends on the specific ticket/customer — the agent must read the issue for a signal rather than assume either path.
